name: PaperPilot retrieval evaluation set
drafted_by: Claude Code, from the PDF text, without running retrieval for these questions
limits: Small set (20 questions, 5 open-access papers, 3 fields). Any Recall@5 from it is a coarse baseline, not a general accuracy figure (RISK-15). Fixed before the first harness run: changes after results are seen must be logged in progress.md.

corpus.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
Investigating the replicability of preclinical cancer biology
Why Most Published Research Findings Are False
Sharing Detailed Research Data Is Associated with Increased Citation Rate
Public Availability of Published Research Data in High-Impact Journals

excluded_probe_queries: What pre-training tasks does the model use?
Does sharing data increase the citation rate?
What proportion of journals require data availability?
positive predictive value of research findings

questions.question: Which optimizer and learning rate were used to pre-train the BERT model?
Does making the network bigger help accuracy on the GLUE benchmark?

expected_quotes.quote: larger models lead to a strict accuracy improvement across all four datasets

questions.question: What share of input words gets hidden at random during the masked-word objective?

expected_quotes.quote: we mask 15% of all WordPiece tokens in each sequence at random

questions.question: How much did effect sizes shrink when preclinical cancer studies were repeated?

expected_quotes.quote: the median effect size in the replications was 85% smaller than the median effect size in the original experiments

questions.question: Does one unsuccessful repeat of a study prove that the original result was wrong?

expected_quotes.quote: a failure to replicate does not disconfirm a finding
A single failure to replicate a finding does not render a verdict on its replicability or credibility

questions.question: How often did repeat studies succeed for results that originally showed no effect?

expected_quotes.quote: for null effects 80% of replications (12/15) were successful on this basis

questions.question: Did studies in living animals reproduce as well as studies without animals?

expected_quotes.quote: animal experiments with positive effects were less likely to replicate

questions.question: Why are results from underpowered, small studies less trustworthy?

expected_quotes.quote: The smaller the studies conducted in a scientific field, the less likely the research findings are to be true

questions.question: What happens to reliability when many groups compete on a fashionable topic?

expected_quotes.quote: The hotter a scientific field (with more scientific teams involved), the less likely the research findings are to be true

questions.question: Is it realistic to run very large studies for every question scientists ask?

expected_quotes.quote: large-scale evidence is impossible to obtain for all of the millions and trillions of research questions posed in current research

questions.question: Where online were most of the shared gene expression datasets hosted?

expected_quotes.quote: Most data sets were located on lab websites

questions.question: Among trials with public data, which properties went along with being cited more?

expected_quotes.quote: only trial design features such as size and clinical endpoint showed a significant association with citation rate

questions.question: What caveat do the authors give about concluding that publishing data causes more citations?

expected_quotes.quote: the demonstrated association does not imply causation

questions.question: How many people extracted the information from the sampled articles?

expected_quotes.quote: Data extraction from the 500 papers was done by a single investigator

questions.question: Did having US federal grants make authors more likely to post their complete raw data?

expected_quotes.quote: the proportion depositing full primary data online was not different when US government funding

questions.question: What was the usual way that articles broke their journal's rules on data?

expected_quotes.quote: most commonly (73%) by not publicly depositing microarray data

questions.question: How much electricity or carbon did training the language model consume?
Did rates of posting research data differ between male and female lead authors?
How does publishing raw data affect citation counts in astronomy?
What was the total budget in dollars of the cancer biology replication project?
